analysis.title: Mutual Fundamentals: Mutual funds remain selective within the AI complex
key_insights: The note covers Q3 2026 quarter-end positioning of 453 large-cap active mutual funds with $3.9 trillion in equity assets, with pricing as of November 18, 2026.

42% of large-cap mutual funds are outperforming their benchmarks YTD versus a historical average of 37%. 81% of large-cap growth funds beat their benchmark, the highest share in over a decade. Only 4% of large-cap value funds beat theirs, the lowest share relative to history.
Value funds have the best absolute YTD return (average fund +14.4% against a Russell 1000 Value benchmark of +23.1%) but trail a rising benchmark. Core funds return 7.4% against 8.1% for the S&P 500.
Mutual fund cash balances are 1.1% of assets at the end of September, matching the December 2025 low. They rose briefly around the start of the US-Iran war and then fell back.

Active US equity mutual funds have roughly $350 billion of outflows YTD and are on track for a 12th consecutive year of outflows. US equity ETFs have about $960 billion of inflows YTD and roughly $210 billion since the start of Q4.
ETF inflows keep GS's Sentiment Indicator positive. Hedge fund equity exposure has declined over the past month.

Mutual funds were underweight AI-exposed equities before the recent weakness in the AI complex. Excluding mega-caps, AI-exposed stocks were 12% of the average fund at the start of Q4, a 130 bp underweight to benchmark weights.

The AI underweight narrowed by 44 bp relative to Q2 (the summary gives 175 bp to 130 bp across Q3). Including mega-caps, AI-exposed equities were 34% of average portfolios against a 40% benchmark weight.

Funds were selective within AI in Q3. The most popular increases include AMD, WDC, STX and SNDK in AI infrastructure and PLTR, SNOW, TWLO, PANW and CRWD in software. The most popular decreases include AMAT, LRCX, CSCO and KLAC.

Large-cap mutual funds are 722 bp underweight the Magnificent 7, essentially unchanged in the quarter. Growth funds are 1002 bp underweight, core funds 731 bp and value funds 434 bp. Part of the underweight stems from diversification restrictions.

The average fund is underweight every Mag 7 name except AMZN, its first average overweight since 2016. A majority of funds cut ownership in each Mag 7 stock except MSFT, with the largest reductions in GOOGL and AAPL.
Only AAPL and AMZN have beaten the equal-weight S&P 500 YTD, and four of the Mag 7 are negative YTD.

High return dispersion and improved market breadth have supported mutual fund performance. Breadth improved through a catch-up from laggards and a modest catch-down from the largest stocks, while dispersion stayed high because higher stock volatility offset higher correlations.

Funds were relatively well positioned for Q4 volatility. Among the top 15 best and worst S&P 500 performers QTD, the average fund was slightly overweight the median best performer and 3 bp underweight the median worst performer.

Largest sector overweights are Industrials (+200 bp), Health Care (+199 bp, a 10-year high) and Financials (+196 bp). The largest underweight is Info Tech (-631 bp), which funds reduced by 29 bp versus Q2.
Overweights in Industrials, Health Care, Energy and Staples rank at or above the 95th percentile of the past 10 years. Tilts to Communication Services and Info Tech sit at the 3rd percentile.
Funds cut Financials the most (-35 bp), led by Banks (-22 bp). JPM, BAC and C were among the 20 most popular Q3 decreases.

Health Care's inverse correlation with the AI trade has raised its popularity during AI volatility. Life Sciences Tools is now the second largest overweight within the sector behind Providers, and RVTY, ILMN and TMO were among the most popular increases.
The Info Tech tilt increase was broad, with the largest additions in Software and Semiconductors. Funds across styles trimmed Consumer Staples and Utilities.

Since the start of Q4 the basket of largest mutual fund overweights (GSTHMFOW) returned +5% versus +3% for the equal-weight S&P 500 and -7% for the largest underweights basket (GSTHMFUW). YTD the underweights basket leads, 16% versus 8%.
Baskets were rebalanced. GSTHMFOW has 13 new constituents including GILD, CRM and NET. GSTHMFUW has 7 new constituents including NFLX, CSCO and PFE.
By net number of funds buying, the three largest Q3 increases were AMD (+57), PLTR (+46) and SNDK (+45). The three largest decreases were GOOGL (-127), JNJ (-108) and AVGO (-105).
risk_factors: The AI complex has struggled since the start of Q4, with names such as INTC, MRVL, SNDK, LRCX and WDC among the worst S&P 500 performers QTD.
Mutual fund Mag 7 underweights partly reflect diversification restrictions, so the tilt does not purely express a view.
Overweight and underweight tilts can be distorted by stock performance and benchmark weights.
Hedge fund equity exposure has declined over the past month, in contrast with continued ETF inflows.
vol_and_positioning: Average large-cap mutual fund cash is 1.1% of assets at the end of September 2026, matching the December 2025 record low.
Average fund is 722 bp underweight the Mag 7 (growth -1002 bp, core -731 bp, value -434 bp), with AMZN the only average overweight, at the first time since 2016.
Average fund is 130 bp underweight AI-exposed equities ex mega-caps, narrowed from earlier in the year. The average fund holds a 12 bp overweight in STX with a net of 30 funds adding.
Sector tilts: Info Tech -631 bp and Communication Services at the 3rd percentile of 10-year history. Health Care at a 10-year high tilt.
Active US equity mutual funds have about $350 billion of YTD outflows against about $960 billion of US equity ETF inflows. Hedge fund equity exposure declined over the past month.
geopolitical: Mutual fund cash balances rose briefly around the start of the US-Iran war before falling back to 1.1% of assets.
